access_evidence: probe openaire_researchproducts_pid: HTTP 200 with numFound/pids/instances when the DOI is passed as a BARE `pid` value; probe openaire_projects_search: HTTP 200 with grant codes on the project side. 60 per-DOI pid lookups -> 59 records.
blockers: `pid=doi:<doi>` and `pid=doi|<doi>` both return numFound=0; only the bare DOI resolves. Verified by matrix in method-development and recorded in the probe note.
historical_depth: publicationDate plus lastUpdateTimeStamp; no creation timestamp, so records are SNAPSHOT_ONLY.
licence_note: OpenAIRE publishes the Graph as open data under CC-BY 4.0 and the Graph API is free to query (https://graph.openaire.eu/docs/). Per-record bestAccessRight and instances[].license are preserved because the publication rights differ from the metadata rights.
machine_interface: REST JSON, Graph API v1 (researchProducts, projects)
name: OpenAIRE Graph API
notes: A pid query can return a record whose `pids` hold no DOI but whose `originalIds` do. The queried DOI is therefore recorded as primary and all others are listed, rather than silently taking the first DOI in the array.
what_is_new: It is the only source here that de-duplicates works across repositories, and the only one that surfaced multiple DOIs for a single work (9 of 59 records). That is directly relevant to de-duplication, and it is also a trap: a naive 'first DOI' reader mis-assigns those records.
